# 4 Maccabees Chapter 11 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** The Mother's Speech and Deaths

---

**11:1** The most admirable mother embraced each of her sons as they were brought forward to die; and she said to them in the ancestral language: My son, have pity on me who carried you nine months in the womb and nursed you three years.

**11:2** I beg you, my child, to look at the sky and the earth and to consider all things that are in them and to know that God made them all out of nothing.

**11:3** And so it is that he is the maker of mankind; and if you turn your heart toward him and receive his consolation, you will live.

**11:4** As for me, I am not afraid of this tyrant; but I will willingly share in these punishments if in doing so I may perhaps be able to shame the tyrant of this world.

**11:5** I am your father, your mother, your nurse, your guide to wisdom, your education; and I urge you: be not afraid, for you did not come into this world apart from the will of God.

**11:6** Think upon this and do not be disheartened, for it is for the law that you are dying.

**11:7** She still says these things while the guards lead her to death.

**11:8** O most wretched of all tyrants! Most barbarous of all tyrants! Does not your heart break when you see how they look at you?

**11:9** Does not pity seize you when you behold the aged mother of seven children being dragged about and treated thus?

**11:10** And yet she bears all this joyfully for the love of God.

**11:11** She is a mother of virtue — for it is God who has implanted virtue in souls.

**11:12** Now indeed, O tyrant, you have put to death these seven sons unjustly.

**11:13** But you have not enslaved their reason, and you have not conquered their virtue.

**11:14** It is you who have been conquered — conquered by reason! And you who rule over all these nations are being overcome by an old woman and her seven sons.

**11:15** The noble mother of the seven, having already witnessed the deaths of all seven of her sons, honored by the memory of them, and having urged them all to a noble death, ended her life nobly in the same way.

**11:16** She acted as though she were making a great festival, glorying in God, so that no one could break her spirit.

**11:17** Let this story suffice for our demonstration of rational devotion mastering even the worst of sufferings.

**11:18** For if a woman and an aged woman and seven brothers were able to overcome the tyrant, it is clear that devotion to God is master of the passions.

**11:19** I have shown this to be true not only in the case of the wise ones I have named, but I have shown it also through the story of the seven brothers and the mother of seven.

**11:20** All of them have proved the sovereignty of reason over the passions.

**11:21** Therefore it is right that I should call them blessed — Eleazar and the seven brothers and their mother.

**11:22** For after all their sufferings and torments and burning, they have conquered. The holy ones reign; they are seated with their father Abraham. Not one of them failed, and not one of them was found wanting.

**11:23** None of the brothers said, Would that I had not come to this! None of them said, Would that I had eaten the defiling food!

**11:24** None of them turned back; none of them shrank from death. Not one of them was deprived of the reward of bravery. From the first to the last, they kept faith and endured.
